info.name: OnlineShop – Requirement 1 (API Design & Security)
info.description:
Ready requests for the Requirement 1 interview. Every request checks its own result, and these checks run after every request:
- path is versioned (/api/v1)
- security headers are present and the Server header is hidden
- every error uses the unified Problem Details format

Run the folders in order (0 → 4): later requests use the tokens and ids saved by earlier ones.
Select the "OnlineShop local" environment first. Wait 1 minute between two full runs (login rate limit).

item.name: 0. API documentation
item.description: The OpenAPI document behind Swagger UI (http://localhost:8080/swagger).

request.description: Swagger UI reads this document. Open http://localhost:8080/swagger in a browser to try every endpoint.

exec: pm.test("Location header points to the new user", () => pm.response.to.have.header("Location"));

item.name: Register customer B (tries to make itself Admin)

request.description: Mass-assignment attempt: the body sends "role": "Admin". The server ignores it, so nobody can register as an admin.

exec: pm.test("\"role\": \"Admin\" in the body is ignored: still a Customer", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().role).to.eql("Customer"));

request.description: The admin account is created at startup from ADMIN_EMAIL / ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env. There is no API that creates an admin.

item.name: Who am I without a token → 401
Forged token: role changed to Admin → 401

request.description: Takes customer A's real token, edits the payload to "role": "Admin" and keeps the old signature. The signature no longer matches, so the token is rejected.

exec: pm.test("The token really was edited to say Admin", () => {

3. Orders
item.description: Create, view, change status. Customer sees only their own orders; only the admin changes status.

pm.test("Total calculated on the server: 2 × 199.99 + 15.50 = 415.48", () => pm.expect(o.totalAmount).to.eql(415.48));

exec: pm.test("Owner still comes from the token", () => pm.expect(o.userId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("userIdA")));

4. Login rate limiting
item.description: Brute-force protection: 5 login attempts per minute per IP, then 429.

request.description: In the Runner this request repeats itself until it gets 429. When clicking Send by hand, press it a few times: 401, 401, ... then 429. Wait 1 minute before logging in again.

exec: pm.test(`Attempt ${attempts}: wrong password → 401`, () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.eql("Invalid email or password."));
pm.test("Blocked with 429 Too Many Requests", () => pm.response.to.have.status(429));
pm.test("Retry-After tells how many seconds to wait", () => pm.response.to.have.header("Retry-After"));

request.description: The limit counts attempts, not failures, so even the right password waits until the minute is over.
